narrative:
The model predicts you have a 21% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your lack of desire to pursue higher education, your clean record of zero past failures, and the fact that your father is your guardian. Surprisingly, your ambition level was the single biggest driver pushing the model toward expecting failure. Because you indicated you do not want to continue studying after this year, the model interpreted this as a major signal that you may not be fully committed to finishing strongly. In contrast, every single student who passed had expressed a clear wish to pursue higher education, so your answer stood out sharply from the successful group.

Having no previous failures worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward passing, as did having your father as guardian. These two elements reduced the risk, but they were not strong enough to overcome the dominant effect of your stated lack of interest in further studies.

To improve your chances, you should seriously reflect on your longer-term goals. Even a small shift in motivation or study habits could make a real difference. Consider talking to a counselor about why higher education feels unimportant right now; addressing that underlying attitude may be the most effective step you can take.
